name: Prize crossword No 24,117
preamble: Solutions with nine letters are of a kind and may lack further definition.

blocks.note: to part is to divide or separate
a ridge is a long stretch of high ground

explanation.surface: An order to split up the hills, perhaps between rival landowners.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says every nine-letter answer is of one kind (birds), so this clue needs no definition: the whole clue is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird, so it belongs to the same family of nine-letter birds named throughout this puzzle.

clue.text: Come up when move is near

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them out of position, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something surfaces just as the next turn in a game approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come up' is read as a past participle, as in 'has come up', which matches the participle form of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are past participles describing something that has risen or appeared, so they swap freely in a sentence.

blocks.note: first meaning: one who tills the soil
second meaning: the bar used to steer a boat

explanation.surface: A farmer has been put in charge of steering something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like one person taking control; in fact the farmer and the steering gear are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tills land is a cultivator, and the steering lever of a small boat carries the same name as that cultivator.

clue.text: Tell doing well at the moment

blocks.note: first meaning: to give someone information
second meaning, read as two words: performing well currently

explanation.surface: Report on somebody who is currently thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN FORM, the answer is the sporting phrase for a player currently performing well.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on knowledge to someone is a synonym of telling, while the split phrase describes current good performance.

definitions.note: an adjective phrase for a noun: the name of the moderate faction of the French Revolution

blocks.note: first meaning: the moderate republican party of the French Revolution, whose deputies came from this region
second meaning: the estuary formed where the Garonne and Dordogne meet near Bordeaux

explanation.walkthrough: The Girondins were the moderate republicans of the French Revolution, named after the department around this Bordeaux estuary; the question mark flags that it is strictly an estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The estuary of the Garonne and Dordogne is a waterway, and its name is shared with the moderate revolutionary party.

blocks.note: corn is trite, sentimental material
C stands for circa, about
a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A dismissive review of corny material about a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble covers the definition: the whole clue is wordplay for one of the puzzle's nine-letter birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a secretive rail of hayfields, one of the birds that make up this puzzle's nine-letter theme.

clue.text: Black stuff for aircraft in vessel

indicators.note: something placed in a container sits inside it, so these letters go within others

blocks.note: tar is black and sticky
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Fuel or tarmac for planes stored in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the preamble, so every word here is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountains and tundra that turns white in winter, one of this puzzle's nine-letter birds.

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong or been spoilt, so the letters are scrambled
what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: A naughty boy gets swallowed by a dog: a cautionary tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the definition, so the clue is all wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the white-headed raptor that serves as the national bird of the United States, fitting the bird theme.

clue.text: Shakespearean ladies in German car, they say

definitions.note: plural because two different Shakespeare plays have a heroine of this name

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: the Porsche is a German sports car, and the name said with a trailing vowel matches

explanation.surface: A pair of Shakespeare's heroines go for a drive in a German sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare has two women with this name: the heiress in The Merchant of Venice and Brutus's wife in Julius Caesar, hence 'ladies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to two separate characters, the clever heiress of Belmont and the wife of Brutus, so one name covers both women.

blocks.note: surface reading: sandwiches and the like eaten outdoors
setter's reading: meals eaten in a meadow, split as two words, which also names a thrush

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words the answer means food eaten out in a field, which is what a picnic is; the preamble supplies the bird definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This large thrush visits Britain in winter, so it joins the other nine-letter birds that form the puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Girl at home on the net?

blocks.note: someone at home is in
a grid is a net of crossing lines

explanation.surface: A young woman who never goes out, spending her time online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The net' suggests the internet, but here it is a mesh of lines, a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use any female first name for 'girl', and this is a Scandinavian woman's name, as in Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Reportedly a drink to help save the planet?

indicators.note: a report is spoken word, so the sound of the phrase counts rather than its spelling

blocks.clueFragment: a drink to help save the planet
blocks.note: Perrier is a brand of sparkling mineral water, and green means environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: A news item about an eco-friendly beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Perrier is a French mineral water brand; an environmentally friendly one would be 'green'. The preamble supplies the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine is the fast-diving falcon, one of the many nine-letter birds this puzzle's theme gathers together.

clue.text: Treatment for bruises sustained in a car

indicators.note: injuries are sustained in a crash, so the words have been knocked about and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remedy for the knocks you picked up in a road accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sustained' reads as describing the bruises, but it signals that the following letters are battered into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: This herbal ointment from a mountain plant is traditionally rubbed on to reduce bruising and swelling.

blocks.note: chaff is light-hearted teasing banter
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Playful banter going on during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it is simply taken as written between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch, so it belongs among the nine-letter birds the preamble declares.

indicators.note: what is found in something lies within it, so these letters go inside another word

blocks.note: C is a musical note
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
a stove is a cooker

explanation.surface: Banknotes, including a large sum, discovered hidden inside an oven.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'note' words give different musical notes, one a letter name and one a sol-fa syllable; the preamble supplies the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock dove is a grey pigeon that nests in tree holes, one of this puzzle's nine-letter birds.

clue.text: Stream drowns Greek filmed with ending first

indicators.note: putting the ending first moves the final letter round to the front
something drowned lies submerged inside the water, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: Zorba the Greek is a 1964 film starring Anthony Quinn
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A film in which a Greek character drowns in a stream, shown with the ending first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek filmed' points to the film title Zorba the Greek. The preamble supplies the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The razorbill is a black-and-white auk with a deep blade-like beak, one of this puzzle's nine-letter birds.

blocks.note: first meaning: the name that follows 'Dirty' in the nickname of a famous TV villain
second meaning: an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A filthy animal's lair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty Den' was Den Watts, the villainous landlord in EastEnders, a long-running British TV soap; 'Dirty' completes his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair where a wild animal lives is called by this word, which is also the soap character's first name.

blocks.note: first meaning: a river in Scotland, and another between England and Wales
second meaning: the spelt-out name of the letter D

explanation.walkthrough: A 'character' can be a letter of the alphabet, and letters have spelt-out names; this is the name of the fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: This British river name matches the written name of a letter, and a letter is a printed character.

indicators.note: to return is to come back the way you went, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A wealthy noble enjoys a healthy profit on an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good return' sounds like a profit, but 'return' signals turning the French word for good backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nob is informal British slang for a person of wealth or high social rank, such as a lord.

clue.text: Best seller over the counter among fish

indicators.note: something among others is surrounded by them, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: OTC is the abbreviation for over the counter, of medicines sold without prescription
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: The top seller at the fishmonger's counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Things that 'sell like hot cakes' sell fast, so one of them is a best seller.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom about selling quickly, the term stands for a product in heavy demand that flies off the shelves.

clue.text: Growth on tree, also known as log, left out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: AKA is the abbreviation of also known as
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A lump on a tree, otherwise called a log, has been omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' looks like one phrase meaning omitted; split it, and 'left' is a letter while 'out' scrambles everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Gall wasps lay eggs in oak buds, which swell into round woody lumps, so this is literally a growth on a tree.

blocks.note: the initials of Elizabeth Barrett Browning, the Victorian poet

explanation.surface: Going on a date with a female poet, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out with' suggests dating; 'with' is only a link, and the poet's initials spell a word for a receding tide.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide retreats from the shore it is said to ebb, which is the sea going out.

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: bother is trouble or fuss
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A family row that ends up flooding over everything.
explanation.walkthrough: A stream is a river here, and R is the map abbreviation for river.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sibling is a family member, and crosswords freely use 'relative' for any kinship term.

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who does business on another's behalf
second meaning: a circumstance that must be taken into account

explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent for consideration' sounds like someone paid a fee; it is two meanings joined by a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial agent who sells goods on commission bears this title, and so does any element weighed in a decision.

indicators.note: a piece is only part of something, so the letters are a portion of longer words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Insignia designed to look like a soldier's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military piece' suggests a gun or an artillery piece, but 'piece' points to a part of the preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is a symbolic device worn or displayed to show allegiance, which is exactly what this answer means.

clue.text: Leggy creature's leader of the country

indicators.note: the leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
rural means relating to the countryside

explanation.surface: A long-legged animal is the head of some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of the country' looks like a head of state; split it after 'leader'. 'Leggy' is used loosely for 'of the legs'.
explanation.definitionFit: This anatomical adjective means relating to the leg or thigh, from the Latin crus, so 'leggy' is a playful stand-in.

clue.text: Get ready for trek of short distance - 9 inches

blocks.note: IN is the abbreviation for inch, a short distance
a span, the width of a spread hand, is nine inches

explanation.surface: Preparing for a journey of just a few inches.
explanation.walkthrough: A trek is the South African word for an ox-wagon journey, and this word is the matching South African verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In South African usage it means to harness oxen or horses to a wagon, which is what you do before setting off.

clue.text: The choice is between one of two numbers or an end of it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.clueFragment: The choice is between one of two numbers
blocks.note: a choice between the Roman numerals for a hundred and a thousand, written out with the word between them
taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dilemma: pick one of two numbers, or else take its end.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two numbers' are Roman numerals, a hundred and a thousand; a choice between them is literally 'C or M'. The preamble supplies the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a dark fish-eating seabird, so it sits with the other nine-letter birds in this themed puzzle.

clue.text: Conference with sailor replacing one in country

indicators.note: to replace is to take the place of something, so one piece swaps in for another

blocks.note: India is a country
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A meeting where a seaman takes someone's place in a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is South African (from Zulu), used for a tribal council or an important meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from Zulu, this South African term means a council or formal gathering to discuss matters, a meeting.

blocks.note: the stammered first letter of the next word
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
taken as written
the rope is what a hanging is carried out with

explanation.surface: A stammering account of a royal accused of a capital offence.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hanging matter' sounds like a capital crime, but here it is the material used, the rope. The preamble supplies the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The phalarope is a small wading bird that spins on water to stir up food, one of this puzzle's nine-letter birds.

clue.text: Warning students of World War I heroine

blocks.note: cave, Latin for beware, was the old schoolboy warning that a teacher was coming
L, for learner, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A cautionary lesson for pupils studying a famous wartime nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave!' (said KAY-vee) was British public-school slang for 'look out'. L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed by the Germans in 1915 for helping Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium.

blocks.note: surface reading: gathering fruit from the hedgerow
setter's reading: blackberries grow on brambles, so going after them is a verb formed from the bush's name, which is also a finch

explanation.walkthrough: Blackberry bushes are brambles, and gathering their fruit is called by a verb made from that name; the preamble supplies the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The brambling is an orange-breasted winter finch, so it completes the set of nine-letter birds in this puzzle.
